Use demonstrations to identify which in-tile feature or count determines the output; do not assume every unusual cell or single marker is positive. 5. For sparse colored diagonal markers on a zero field, identify the invariant of their parallel lines: constant row−column for down-right diagonals, or row+column for down-left diagonals. Use zero-based row/column coordinates and verify the sign convention against observed output: for down-right stripes, `column−row` indexes the phase; for down-left stripes, `row+column` does. Infer the smallest plausible period and color per phase by checking which candidate periods avoid assigning different colors to the same residue; use demo output to establish the complete mapping when available. Then color every cell from its phase, rather than preserving only the sparse markers. Verify several cells against each demonstrated line and ensure the resulting output reproduces every demo. Do not assume the marker positions alone give every residue's color; use output examples to establish the complete mapping.

It may be a solid suffix or only selected motif-phase positions. Color only the confirmed missing continuation cells; preserve the existing motif and unrelated cells.
